penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Code remediation as a service requires per-repo, per-codebase human judgment to triage and fix findings in any meaningful way beyond a basic lint report. A fully automated audit report is buildable, but the value proposition customers would actually pay for (remediation, not just flagging) requires human engineering work.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Engineering teams evaluating a code quality tool will have questions about false positives, integration with their CI pipeline, and tuning rules — requiring meaningful support effort per customer.

rationale: The buyer is real and well-defined — engineering managers and CTOs at companies using AI coding tools already pay for SonarQube and CodeClimate — and the pain (accumulating AI-generated technical debt) is a genuine, recurring business cost. However, once the penalties for per-customer fulfillment and support load are applied, the total falls below the validate threshold. More critically, operational_autonomy scores only 5: a pure AI-lint-report product is buildable autonomously, but that version is commodity and unlikely to command real revenue; the version customers would pay meaningfully for requires human engineering judgment to remediate, which breaks the factory's autonomy model. This is a venture-backed DevTools company idea, not a solo operator microservice.
solution_plan: What it is: an AI code-quality audit report service that scans a repo and flags structural patterns common in AI-generated code (poor test coverage, God functions, missing error handling, copy-paste duplication). Build: the factory connects a Claude prompt chain to GitHub API access, runs static analysis heuristics, and generates a scored PDF/HTML report; a Stripe payment link and a simple intake form (GitHub repo URL + email) are all that's needed. Sell: reach engineering leads via LinkedIn outreach targeting 'Head of Engineering' at companies that list Cursor or Copilot in their job postings; outreach batches require operator approval before sending. Maintain: report generation is fully automated; however, customers expecting actionable remediation (not just flagging) will demand human follow-up, which a solo non-technical operator cannot realistically deliver. The gap between what Claude can automate (the report) and what customers would pay premium rates for (the fix) is too wide for this model — recommend dropping unless scoped to a very minimal one-time audit report at a low price point, which would face a commoditized market.
notes: operational_autonomy gate unmet (score 5, floor 7). The buildable version (automated report) is low-value commodity; the valuable version (remediation service) requires per-customer human engineering work. Drop unless scoped to pure self-serve report product at a price point where autonomy is preserved.
